overview: This enum selects the grade of artwork shown for a character emblem on a player card.

None.simple: An empty grade that selects no emblem artwork.
None.technical: Declared as the zero value of the uint8 enum and assigned by the FGameDataTableRow_PlayerCardEmblem constructor. UGamePlayerCardEmblemWidget::SetEmblem casts the row grade to uint8 and passes it to PlayerCard_FindEmblemItemId, which requires an exact byte match with Id_Character. No exported emblem row has this grade, so the default alone resolves no emblem item.

Grade1.simple: The first grade of player-card emblem artwork.
Grade1.technical: Declared as uint8 slot 1. The export has 29 PlayerCardEmblemDataTable rows with this grade. UGamePlayerCardEmblemWidget::SetEmblem passes the grade as a uint8 to PlayerCard_FindEmblemItemId along with the row Id_Character. That finder takes the first emblem row with an exact character and grade match, then the first Emblem Item whose VariableId equals that row Id. The Item Id selects the texture from EmblemParameterMap. No grade ordering or unlock rule is stored in this row.

Invalid.simple: A reserved invalid marker for emblem grades.
Invalid.technical: Declared as the uint8 slot 255 in the enum header. No reconstructed consumer compares GradeType with Invalid, and no exported emblem row carries it. Its behavior in PlayerCard_FindEmblemItemId is therefore unresolved.

notes: FGameDataTableRow_PlayerCardEmblem defaults GradeType to None. The export has 113 rows across Grade1 through Grade4 and no None or Invalid row.
Each (Id_Character, GradeType) pair is unique in the export, so the grade acts as a discriminator that picks one emblem row and then one Emblem Item row per character.
The grade is passed as a plain uint8 to the finder, so its only observed operation is byte equality. Storage of unlock state and textures lives in the Item row and the widget parameter map.
The display path calls the finder with bUnlockedOnly set to false, so ownership does not gate the emblem shown on a player card.
No named alias or unused numeric slot appears in this enum.
